recoveryCodesLowHint: Running low. Generate a new set so you don't get locked out.
recoveryCodesError: Could not generate new recovery codes. Try again.

sessions.revokeBody: That browser will need to sign in again. Nothing else about the account changes.
sessions.revokeAllBody: This ends {count} other sessions. You'll stay signed in here.
sessions.revokedAll: Every other session was signed out.
sessions.revokeError: Could not sign that session out. Try again.
sessions.needsVerification: For your security, this needs a fresh verification first.

devices.title: Devices
devices.hint: Where you're signed in, and which browsers are trusted. Verifying on one trusts it for 14 days; anything else is asked for a code when it signs in.
devices.truncatedNotice: Showing your most recently seen devices — older ones aren't listed.
devices.forgetUntrusted: Forget {count, plural, one {# untrusted device} other {# untrusted devices}}
devices.forgetUntrustedBody: {count, plural, one {The device you haven't verified on recently} other {The # devices you haven't verified on recently}} will be removed from this list. Trusted devices stay.
devices.forgetUntrustedDone: {count, plural, =0 {No devices needed forgetting} one {# device forgotten} other {# devices forgotten}}
devices.removeBody: It's signed out and forgotten, and will be asked for a code the next time it signs in.

activity.title: Security activity
activity.hint: Recent changes and checks on this account.

step_up.enrollment_prompted: Asked to add a second step
step_up.new_device_detected: Signed in from a new device

posture.exposedTitle: Your password is the only thing protecting this account
posture.exposedBody: Anyone who learns it is in. Adding a second step takes about two minutes and stops that outright.
posture.basicBody: A stolen password alone won't get anyone in. A passkey would also block the fake login pages that codes can't.
posture.strongBody: Nothing to type means nothing to phish. Add an authenticator app as a backup for when your device isn't to hand.
posture.maximumBody: A passkey for everyday sign-in and an authenticator app to fall back on. Nothing more to do here.

title: Settings
subtitle: Manage your personal account and preferences
workspaceHint: Appearance, app behavior, and connected services.
helpHint: Restart the guided tour whenever you need it.
aiHint: What the assistant can see, where it goes, and who else can see it.
accountHint: This information applies to you only and is visible to colleagues.
dateOfBirthHint: Only the day and month are ever shown, and only if you turn this on — your birth year always stays private.
editProfileHint: Update the details colleagues see about you.
profileGradientHint: The color behind your picture on your profile and in the directory.
avatarHint: Any photo works — it's cropped to a square for you.
sessionHint: Ending your session here, and what happens to the account itself.
signOutHint: Ends this session on this device. Other devices stay signed in — end those under Active sessions.
exportDataHint: A JSON file with your profile, preferences, notifications, tickets, suggestions and AI history.
deleteAccountHint: Accounts can't be deleted from here. Access is tied to your employment, so IT or an admin closes the account when it ends — ask them if you need it removed sooner.
completenessHint: Add a photo, job title, department and phone number so colleagues can find and reach you.
appPrefsHint: Saved to your account — they follow you across devices.
connectionsHint: Whether your account is linked to the systems that feed your absences and activity.
clockodoDirect: Linked directly — your absences sync automatically.
clockodoViaPerson: Linked via your ActivityTrack record — your absences sync automatically.
clockodoUnlinkedHint: Ask an admin to link your Clockodo account so absences sync.
clockodoMigrationError: Could not migrate the Clockodo link
personUnlinkedHint: No ActivityTrack person record is linked to you yet.
avatarPreviewHint: Your photo is cropped to a square and resized automatically.
passkeysHint: Use a fingerprint, face scan, or device PIN to sign in.
passkeySignInHint: Choose a passkey saved on this device or another nearby device.
addPasskeyHint: Choose a name, then confirm with your device.
renamePasskeyHint: Choose a name that helps you recognize this passkey.
removePasskeyHint: This passkey will no longer be able to sign in.
passkeySignInError: Could not sign in with that passkey
totpHint: Use an app like Google Authenticator or 1Password to generate sign-in codes.
replaceTotp: Set up a new authenticator app
totpNeedsRotation: You used a recovery code, so this authenticator counts as lost. Set up a new one to get your second factor back.
setUpTotpHint: Scan the code with your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code it shows.
totpQrAlt: QR code for authenticator app setup
removeTotpHint: You'll no longer be asked for a code from this app.
totpEnabledHint: An authenticator app is set up on this account.
totpNotEnabled: No authenticator app set up yet.
totpLoadError: Could not load authenticator app status
totpEnrollError: Could not start authenticator app setup
totpCodeError: That code didn't match — check the time on your device
totpRecoveryCodesHint: Each code can be used once to sign in if you lose access to your authenticator app. Store them somewhere safe — you won't see them again.
secondaryEmailsHint: Other addresses you can be reached at, like a work address for Performance. Verified ones can be used for sign-in and password resets.
secondaryEmailsFootnote: Up to 5. You'll be asked to confirm it's you before adding one.
addSecondaryEmailHint: We'll send a 6-digit code to this address to confirm you own it.
secondaryEmailCodeHint: Enter the code we sent to {email}.
secondaryEmailAddError: Could not send a code to that address
removeSecondaryEmailHint: You'll no longer be able to use this address for sign-in or password resets.
securityAlwaysMfaHint: Ask for a verification code every time you sign in, on top of your usual sign-in method. Off by default — most people don't need this.
securityAlwaysMfaPasskeyWarning: You already have a passkey, which is already very strong on its own. Turning this on will ask for a code every time you sign in, even with your passkey — most people don't need this.
securityAlwaysMfaEnabled: MFA will now be required at every sign-in
securityAlwaysMfaDisabled: MFA is no longer required at every sign-in
securityDeviceTrackingHint: Skip the extra sign-in check on devices you've verified on in the last 14 days. When off, nothing about your devices is stored and every sign-in asks for a code.
securityAreaHint: Performance and the HR vault use your intranet account instead of their own password, and ask you to verify again every 14 days.
securityAreaApplicantVault: Verify more often for the HR vault
securityAreaAlwaysStepUpHint: Ask again after 8 hours instead of every 14 days.
securityDeviceTrackingOffBody: Your recognized devices will be forgotten, and every new sign-in will ask for a verification code.
trashHint: Bring back something deleted in the last 30 days.
trashSectionHint: Kept for 30 days, then removed for good.
trashEmptyHint: Deleted announcements, tickets, pages and posts wait here for 30 days.
